page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4a server family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 CPU architecture. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on an arm64 architecture, the n4a-standard-32 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that can leverage ARM-based instruction sets. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core instances. However, users should note the absence of local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, x86-specific CPU flags and vector extensions such as AVX, AMX, and FMA are not supported on this hardware.

With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include web serving, application servers, microservices architectures, containerized deployments, and medium-scale databases that do not require local SSD performance or GPU acceleration.
